contexts.text: I am God Shaddai () in the sense of the letter, = the name of Abraham's god, by which name the Lord was first represented before them. Explained.
They had lost the name Jehovah, and worshipped Shaddai... I appeared unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as god Shaddai ().
Thus Abraham (at first) was an idolater, and had not as yet rejected the god Shaddai.
The reason the Lord was willing to be represented by the name Shaddai is that He never wants to suddenly destroy the worship implanted from infancy. Explained.
Translators render Shaddai, the Almighty; others, the Thunderer; but it properly signifies the Tempter, and the Benefactor after temptations; as is evident in Job. Illustrated.
The word shaddai itself signifies vastation, thus temptation.
As it originated from nations in Syria, He is not called Elohim Shaddai, but El Shaddai; and in Job simply Shaddai.

As there is comfort after temptations, they attributed the consequent good to the same Shaddai; and also the understanding of truth which is thence. Illustrated. And as He was thus held to be a god of truth the name was retained in the Prophets, but by Shaddai, there, is meant truth. Illustrated.
Isaac and Jacob also name the god Shaddai in a like sense: as one who tempts, and delivers from temptation, and afterwards benefits. Illustrated.

The worship of Shaddai originated from (their being) heard Spirits who reproved, and who afterwards comforted... They named the reproving Spirit Shaddai; and, as he afterwards comforted, the god Shaddai. Explained.
For the Lord is represented by the God Shaddai whom Abraham worshipped.

God Shaddai will bless thee () = the temptations of that truth and good through which is conjunction. God Shaddai = temptations... because in ancient times they distinguished the supreme God, or the Lord, by various names, according to His attributes...

As to God Shaddai, in special, the Lord had been so called in the Ancient Church relatively to temptations, and to blessings and benefits after them. Hence it is that by God Shaddai, in the internal sense, are signified temptations.
Those of the Ancient Church distinguished the Divine by various names... as God Shaddai, from temptations, in which the Lord fights for man, and after which benefits him.
I am God Shaddai () = the state of temptation past, and now Divine comfort; for God Shaddai = temptation and comfort afterwards...
Vastation from Shaddai () = vastation in temptations.
And God Shaddai () = consolation after hard things; for Shaddai = temptation and consolation after it.

The Ancients distinguished the only God by various names... and as they believed temptations to be from Him, they called God, then, Shaddai, and by this name understood not another god, but the only one as to temptations. But when the Ancient Church had declined, they began to worship as many gods as there had been names of the only God... each family having its own god... and the family of Terah worshipped Shaddai as theirs. AC 6003:end.
The reason not temptation only, but also consolation, is signified by Shaddai, is that consolation follows all spiritual temptations.
And with Shaddai () = the Lord the Benefactor after temptations. AE 448:6.
I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob in God Shaddai () = the Lord's temptations as to the human, and the temptations of the faithful, and afterwards consolations.
The finality of Divine truth in Heaven (is also signified by) his voice as... the voice of Shaddai ()... because God Shaddai = truth rebuking in temptations, and afterwards comforting. AE 283:13.
Shaddai () = a state of temptations.
Temptations are signified by the discipline of Shaddai ().
Shaddai, etc. are names of one God... but each = some attribute.
